title: Spike: a publication repo consumes Papyrus from packages and deploys CMS + backend + staging (Pilobol.us)
description: Phase 1 spike per docs/standard-site.md (PR #98). Prove, on a scratch copy of the Pilobol.us setup, that a publication repo can depend on Papyrus through packages (papyrus-newsroom on PyPI; @anthusai/papyrus and @anthusai/papyrus-infra on npm) and build/deploy its newsroom CMS app + Amplify Gen 2 backend + a staging site on Amplify. NOT allowed: publishing to the public registries (use local packs / wheels), touching production apps (pilobol.us d1od6t7lzbwanr, newsroom.pilobol.us d11eu9hbs2mipk, p.apyr.us dbsyytcm9drqa, anth.us d2hbn1ig6nqyhy, TI d3on1y5vlrxmam). Acceptance checklist at the end of docs/standard-site.md.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
SPIKE RESULT (PPY-82be6c), restart run 2026-10-05. Branch feature/PPY-82be6c-package-spike (PR into develop, not merged). Scratch publication repo: github.com/AnthusAI/papyrus-spike-pkg (private, not connected to Amplify). Nothing published to npm/PyPI; packages are a local `npm pack` tarball (@anthusai/papyrus 0.1.0-next.6) and a local wheel (papyrus-newsroom 0.1.0.dev6, same version mapped to PEP 440). Papyrus is the two-package shape of PR #99: infra ships inside @anthusai/papyrus as `@anthusai/papyrus/infra`, aws-cdk-lib and constructs are optional peers.

VERDICT: the packaging approach WORKS WITH CHANGES (route-shim option A for the app, `defineSiteBackend` option A for the backend; no need for the option B fallback). The changes are listed at the end.

(a) PASS. One tarball (668 KB packed, 20 routes). Fresh `npm install` of tarball+next+react: 788 packages, `npm ls aws-cdk-lib constructs` is empty, node_modules 814 MB (next 158 MB, @next/swc 127 MB, mermaid 90 MB, lucide 46 MB). The publication repo with Amplify backend dev deps (which pull aws-cdk-lib 151 MB, @aws-amplify 575 MB): 1.8 GB.
(b) PASS. publication/brand.ts + papyrus.config.ts `defineSite({ brands: [...], defaultBrand })`; no Papyrus edit. SiteBrandId/ThemePackId are `string`.
(c) PASS (caveat). `next build` OK (log: Papyrus-spike/logs/pub2-build-*.log). Page renders data-site-brand="pilobolus-pub", the publication theme tokens and title. With the Pilobol.us-style brand (`newsroomBasePath: ""`) `/newsroom` 307s to `/` (existing middleware behaviour), so "/newsroom loads" means "/" for that brand. Only HTML checked, no login flow in a browser.
(d) PASS. `ampx sandbox --identifier spike2` from the publication's `amplify/backend.ts` (`export default defineSiteBackend(site)`): ~9.5 min, all stacks created. Python Lambdas (knowledge-query, email-submission-processor, slack-delivery; python3.12/arm64) bundled by `pip install papyrus-newsroom==0.1.0.dev6 --platform manylinux2014_aarch64 --only-binary --find-links vendor` plus handler.py from the npm package. Invoked papyrus-knowledge-query: HTTP 200, structured result (no import errors). Real fix for the tactus problem: pyproject `tactus >=0.52,<1` (PyPI 0.52.0) in the `newsroom` extra; `file://` removed, wheel METADATA has no file:/git+ requirement, `package-mode = false` and `{include="publications"}` removed, poetry.lock regenerated (`poetry check --lock` ok). limatus 0.17.x and 0.29.0 both resolve. anthus-markus 0.5.1 on PyPI (Anthus AI Solutions) matches git tag v0.5.1: all 15 .py files byte-identical to the tag. NOT done: the console-responder container image and SES/Slack/backup features (disabled in the scratch config).
(e) PASS. Guest (identityPool, signed out) reads a seeded PublishedItem through Papyrus's ContentRepository from the Next server (HTTP 200), and the draft slug returns 404.
(f) PASS, 12/12 (scripts/spike-auth-test.mjs, test users created and deleted in the script, random in-memory password, nothing printed): editor reads draft Item; guest and authenticated non-editor get Unauthorized on Item; staging route: anonymous redirected with no draft, non-editor gets the 403 page, editor gets the draft with STAGING banner. Enforcement is AppSync, not the page. Not tested: noindex/robots/banner guards (SITE_ENV), static (Markus) drafts export.
(g) PASS. Without the CDK, importing `@anthusai/papyrus/infra` (and `papyrus-infra synth`) fails with: "@anthusai/papyrus/infra needs aws-cdk-lib and constructs, which are optional peer dependencies. Install them in the package that imports this entry (your infra/ folder)...". A separate infra/ app with the tarball + aws-cdk-lib + constructs imports it and `papyrus-infra synth --site site.json` produces the app-shell template (Amplify App/Branch/Domain, 2 roles). Synth only, nothing deployed.
(h) PARTIAL. Local simulation of the WEB_COMPUTE frontend steps from a clean copy (no node_modules/.next): `npm ci` from the tarball, `ampx generate outputs --stack <backend>` (the frontend-only/staging pattern), `npm run build`: PASS. Not testable without Amplify: the real build image and the GitHub App connection, `ampx pipeline-deploy`, branch deployments against another branch's backend.
Also: clean venv `pip install "papyrus-newsroom[markus]"` + Markus reader build from a copy of Pilobol.us content (12 pages) works with no checkout/PAPYRUS_ROOT.

WHAT BROKE / NOT AS DESIGNED (changes docs/standard-site.md must make)
1. Backend entry must ship compiled JS: Node refuses to type-strip .ts under node_modules (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING) and ampx's tsx does not rescue it. stage.mjs compiles amplify/** (not handlers; esbuild bundles those) and define-site to ESM .js beside the TS. Doc 1.4 says "imports from node_modules resolve": add this.
2. Python deps: the `papyrus` CLI imports `limatus` at import time (papyrus_content/editorial_*.py), so the base install cannot run the CLI. Either make limatus a base dependency or lazy-import it. `papyrus_content.markus_renderer` works with base + [markus]. Also `anthus-markus` is the `markus` extra, and dev installs need `poetry install --all-extras`.
3. Amplify's AL2023 build image defaults to Python 3.10 (AWS docs; not verified on a real build) while papyrus-newsroom requires >=3.12: a reader build that pip-installs it needs python3.12 provisioned. Lambda bundling is unaffected because it uses `--python-version 3.12 --ignore-requires-python`. Also pip prints dependency-conflict noise from the host env on --target installs (harmless).
4. npm lockfile: a lock updated incrementally (swapping the tarball) failed `npm ci` ("Missing: @opentelemetry/core@2.0.0 from lock file"); regenerating from scratch fixed it. Add `npm ci --dry-run` to CI and Renovate guidance.
5. Sizes: infra/ "small app" is not small: 990 MB, because @anthusai/papyrus lists all Next/runtime packages as dependencies. Consider an infra-only entry or accept it.
6. The tarball still contains 16 `publications/*` files (TI/anth-us/pilobol-us brands) because lib/site-brand.ts imports built-ins (C1 is unresolved by this spike; the three brands must leave core in Phase 2).
7. Auth rules: a signed-in non-editor cannot read PublishedItem over userPool (rules are guest/identityPool and editor/admin only). SSR for logged-in non-editors must use identityPool for Published* and userPool only for drafts.
8. Test harness: seven .cjs tests (own TS require hook) broke on the new `papyrus-site` alias; fixed with scripts/register-papyrus-aliases.cjs. Pre-existing failures unchanged: test:newsroom (forum routes), test:theme-packs, test:newsroom-card-layout (they fail on develop too). `tsc --noEmit` clean.
9. The `amplify.yml` for the publication used `npm ci` and `ampx pipeline-deploy`; build specs from the CDK shell still need verifying on Amplify.

NEEDS RYAN: the Amplify GitHub App handshake for the scratch repo or any real publication repo (without it, cannot test: Amplify build from the repo, `ampx pipeline-deploy`, staging branch vs production backend outputs, deploy-on-push); npm scope `@anthusai` ownership and name availability at first publish; a decision on #2 (limatus base vs lazy); deleting the scratch repo AnthusAI/papyrus-spike-pkg when done.

AWS: created (all `amplify-spike2papyruspkg-spike2-sandbox-*`, us-east-1, acct 335163751677): the sandbox stack set (auth/Cognito user + identity pool, AppSync API, DynamoDB tables via Amplify, S3 media + vector buckets, ~20 Lambdas, IAM roles), 2 Cognito test users (deleted by the test script) and seeded Items (deleted by the script). Deleted: `ampx sandbox delete --identifier spike2` (first attempt DELETE_FAILED on AppSync resolver nested stacks, second attempt completed), then 6 leftover Lambda log groups deleted by hand. Final read-only verification (CloudFormation stacks containing "spike" not DELETE_COMPLETE, Lambda, Cognito user/identity pools, AppSync, S3, S3 Vectors, DynamoDB, IAM roles, Amplify apps, SSM, log groups): all empty. The old `spikepapyruspkg` stacks were gone before deploying (the other agent had finished). The earlier sandbox's local outputs are not reused.

ESTIMATE, real Pilobol.us migration onto packages (CMS app + backend + staging gate, excluding the Phase 2 content importer/exporter and Markus reader snapshot): about 4-6 working days once the Phase 2 items land: release pipeline + extras fixes (1-1.5), move brand/config into the repo and register (0.5), repo scaffold + infra/site.json + GitHub App + replacing the app-shell PAT (1-1.5), CMS app on Amplify with backend pipeline and verification against production data (1-1.5), staging branch + Cognito gate + SITE_ENV guards (1). Biggest risk: reconnecting live app d11eu9hbs2mipk without rebuilding the backend.

comments.text: PR #100 merged to develop. Spike verdict: packaging works with changes (7 doc changes listed in the PR body). Scratch AWS resources verified deleted; scratch repo AnthusAI/papyrus-spike-pkg and local Papyrus-spike/ pending Ryan's OK to delete.

comments.text: Follow-ups from the spike merged: #101 (CI installs the newsroom extra and typescript; limatus is a base dependency; first green Inbound email tests run since June). Scratch repo AnthusAI/papyrus-spike-pkg deleted. Remaining from the spike report (docs/standard-site.md updates): compiled backend entry, Python 3.12 on Amplify build image, npm ci --dry-run in CI, SSR must use identityPool for published and userPool for drafts, remove built-in publications/* from the tarball in Phase 2.

right_now_summary: The spike proved package-based deployment works, and cleanup is complete; only documentation follow-ups remain.
